standards.title: Every tool declares the scope it needs and whether it has a side effect
standards.why: Access reviews and least privilege start from what a tool can do, not from what an agent is told.

standards.title: Code decides; models read and write
standards.why: A recommendation that changes a release follows rules an engineering change board can read and test.

standards.title: Models are reached only through the platform client
standards.why: Cost, logging, data residency and model choice are governed in one place.

standards.title: Every figure in user-facing text traces to a source
standards.why: An invented number in an engineering report is worse than no report.

standards.title: Untrusted text is guarded before a model reads it
standards.why: Supplier notes and documents can carry instructions; they are data.

standards.title: Domain-model predictions carry an interval and an input check
standards.why: A surrogate may decide only where it is calibrated and has seen similar inputs.

standards.title: Releases need signatures from different people
standards.why: No agent releases a change; people with the required roles do.

standards.title: Evaluated before production
standards.why: A solution ships with an evaluation suite, and its last run meets the safety thresholds.

standards.title: Model names and prompts come from configuration
standards.why: Pinned, reviewable versions; no silent model changes in code.
